title: "My servant the Branch" and the stone with seven eyes (Zech 3:8–10)
speaker: The angel of the LORD (for the LORD of Armies)
description: Joshua and his colleagues are a sign that the LORD will bring his servant the Branch; the stone with seven eyes will be engraved and the land's iniquity removed in one day; then every man will invite his neighbour under vine and fig tree.
in_text_interpretation: The Branch is not named here; Zech 6:12 says "the man whose name is the Branch … shall build the temple of the LORD".

interpretations.label: The Branch is the Messiah (the Davidic Sprout)
proponents: C. F. Keil (1868): Tsemach is "simply a proper name of the Messiah", as "my servant David" in Ezekiel
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Branch/Sprout is a Davidic-Messianic title in Jeremiah (23:5; 33:15); removing iniquity "in one day" is the Messiah's work (Keil). Christian readers apply it to Jesus. Objection: Mitchell holds that for Zechariah the Shoot is Zerubbabel and that 3:8b is a later gloss.

interpretations.label: The Branch is Zerubbabel; 3:8b is a later gloss
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Zerubbabel was already in Jerusalem and working, so he could not be "brought"; the clause was added by a later reader; 6:12 originally crowned Zerubbabel as the Shoot and was recast for Joshua.
